s: Under whom was Numaish (All India Industrial Exhibition), Hyderabad, first held in 1938?
x: Numaish was first held in 1938 by the 7th Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan.

s: Where did the Nagoba Jatara 2026 begin on 18 January?
x: Nagoba Jatara began at Keslapur in Indravelli mandal, Adilabad; Medaram hosts the Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara.

s: Which festival began on 16 January 2026 at Spituk Monastery near Leh, featuring Cham masked dances?
x: Spituk Gustor is held at Spituk Monastery near Leh and features Cham masked dances.

s: Kathputli puppets of Rajasthan generally use how many strings?
x: Kathputli puppets use 2–5 strings, not 5–8.

s: Bagurumba, in the news for a performance by more than 10,000 artists, is associated with which community and State?
x: Bagurumba is associated with the Bodo community of Assam, and more than 10,000 artists performed it. The Hatti tribe belongs to the Boda Tyohar tradition, not Bagurumba.

s: The 39th Surajkund International Crafts Mela was held at which place?
x: The 39th Surajkund International Crafts Mela was held in Faridabad, Haryana. Jaisalmer was associated with the Jain Chadar Mahotsav, while Rusoma hosted the Rusoma Orange Festival.

s: The Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara is regarded as which of the following?
o: Asia's largest tribal congregation, and India's second-largest after the Kumbh
Asia's second-largest tribal congregation, and India's largest after the Kumbh
Asia's largest tribal congregation, and India's largest after the Kumbh
Asia's second-largest tribal congregation, and India's second-largest after the Kumbh
x: The Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara is regarded as Asia's largest tribal congregation and the largest in India after the Kumbh. The other options change one or both of these rankings.

s: Which of the following about the Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara is NOT correct?
o: It commemorates resistance against Mughal taxation.
It is associated with the Magha full moon.
It is a biennial festival held at Medaram in Mulugu.
x: The Jatara commemorates resistance against Kakatiya taxation, not Mughal taxation.

s: Boda Tyohar is identified as the largest festival of which tribal community in Sirmaur?
x: Boda Tyohar is the largest festival of the Hatti tribe in Sirmaur, Himachal Pradesh. Bodo is associated with Bagurumba, while Gond and Toda are not identified with Boda Tyohar here.

s: Which was the partner country of the 39th Surajkund International Crafts Mela?
x: Egypt was the partner country of the 39th Surajkund Mela at Faridabad.

s: The Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara honours deities of which tribe?
x: Sammakka and Saralamma are Koya tribal deities; the jatara recalls resistance to Kakatiya taxation.

s: In which district is Medaram, the venue of the Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara?
x: The biennial Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara is held at Medaram in Mulugu district, Telangana.

s: Which clan carries Godavari water for the Nagoba Jatara at Keslapur?
x: The Mesram clan of Gonds carries Ganga water 70 km from Hasthinamadugu on the Godavari.

s: Bhupatipur, where 12 Palaeolithic stone tools about 100,000–40,000 years old were found, is in which district?
x: Bhupatipur is in Kannayigudem, Mulugu district, Telangana; the tools are about 100,000–40,000 years old.

s: Under which mission is 'Na Ooru – Na Vaarasatvam', a Ministry of Culture project?
x: Na Ooru – Na Vaarasatvam is a Ministry of Culture project under the National Mission on Cultural Mapping.

s: The bandhgala originated in which princely state, under the Rathore dynasty?
x: The bandhgala originated in Jodhpur under the Rathores; its precursor was the Achkan, and it is indigenous, not colonial, in origin.

s: Whom does the Bucheshwara temple at Koravangala (1173 CE) honour?
x: Bucheshwara at Koravangala dates to 1173 CE and honours Veera Ballala II.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about heritage and archaeological findings in February 2026?
o: Tyonda in Jhunjhunu yielded 11th–12th century temple remains with Lakshmi and Ganesha
The mature phase of Bhirrana dates to 3600–2900 BCE
The Falcon Living Museum is a Mizo heritage village near Aizawl documented by INTACH
x: The mature phase of the Bhirrana settlement dates to 2600–1900 BCE.

s: With which deity is the Chennakeshava temple at Belur associated?
x: The Chennakeshava temple at Belur is associated with Vishnu, not Shiva.

s: In which year did the Serengsia battle, part of the Ho tribal resistance in West Singhbhum, take place?
x: The Serengsia battle took place in 1837, not 1831.

s: Which of the following Hoysala monuments is a 12th-century stepwell?
x: Hulikere Kalyani is a 12th-century stepwell; the others are temples.

s: Which method, in which the hull is stitched first and the ribs added later, was used to build INSV Kaundinya?
x: INSV Kaundinya used the Tankai method of stitching the hull first and adding the ribs later.

s: According to tradition, who built the Somnath temple of silver in the Treta yuga?
x: Tradition holds Treta yuga – silver by Ravana; Satya – gold by Chandra, Dvapara – wood by Krishna, Kali – stone by Bhimdev Solanki.

s: From the roots of which tree are Meghalaya's living root bridges, nominated as the "Jingkieng Jri" cultural landscape, made?
x: The living root bridges are made from the roots of the rubber fig, not bamboo.

s: The world’s oldest cave art, a hand stencil dating to at least 67,800 years ago, was found at which place?
x: The hand stencil was found at Muna in Sulawesi, Indonesia, and is at least 67,800 years old. Lakkundi, Jehanpora and Piprahwa are associated with archaeological findings in India.

s: What does the bow of INSV Kaundinya carry?
x: The bow carries the Simha Yali, while the sails bear the Gandabherunda and the Sun.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: About 30 Indian inscriptions of the 1st–3rd centuries CE have been found in Egypt's Valley of the Kings
The name “Cikai Korran” occurs 8 times in these inscriptions
Chennakeshava Temple, Belur is part of UNESCO's “Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas” (2023)
x: The ASI was established in 1861; 1984 is the year INTACH was established.

s: Who founded the Hoysala dynasty?
x: The Hoysala dynasty (11th–14th century CE) was founded by Nripa Kama II.

s: Which of the following was included in UNESCO’s 2023 World Heritage inscription titled “Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas”?
x: Chennakeshava at Belur was one of the three components of the UNESCO 2023 Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas. Bucheshwara, Lakshmidevi and Hulikere Kalyani are different Hoysala-associated monuments.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the three bronzes being returned by the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art?
o: They include a 16th-century Vijayanagara bronze of Sundarar and Paravai
They include a 10th-century Chola Shiva Nataraja
The Shiva Nataraja among them is a 16th-century Vijayanagara bronze
x: The Shiva Nataraja is a 10th-century Chola bronze; the 16th-century Vijayanagara piece is Sundarar and Paravai.

s: To which port did INSV Kaundinya make its maiden overseas voyage from Porbandar?
x: INSV Kaundinya sailed from Porbandar to Muscat; its design is based on a ship in the Ajanta paintings.

s: With reference to Srimanta Sankardeva, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sankardeva came from the Siromani Bhuyans. He lived 1449–1568, went on pilgrimage in 1481 and composed his first Borgeet at Badarikashrama (Badrinath).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about heritage and archaeology in news?
o: A coin and stamp were issued in New Delhi on 16 February 2026 for the Ol Chiki centenary
The Konark Sun Temple sanctum reopened after 120 years
The Devnimori site is in Aravalli district of Gujarat
The Seva Teerth complex was inspired by the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur
x: The Konark sanctum reopened after 122 years, not 120 years.

s: The 9-foot Bhairava sculpture reported in February 2026 was found at which location?
x: The 9-foot Bhairava sculpture was found at Raichakonda Fort in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Telangana. Begili is associated with the Chola Shiva temple, while Jaisalmer and Rusoma were venues of other events.

s: Which exhibition opened in New Delhi to mark the return of the Piprahwa relics after about 125 years?
x: The exhibition was titled 'The Light and the Lotus'; the Piprahwa relics were found in 1898 at Siddharthnagar, UP, and are linked to Kapilavastu.

s: A nearly 900-year-old Chola Shiva temple was found under mango tree roots at which place?
x: The nearly 900-year-old Chola Shiva temple was found at Begili, near Hosur, in Krishnagiri. Raichakonda Fort is associated with the Bhairava sculpture, while Jaisalmer and West Singhbhum relate to separate events.

s: Which archaeological site, formerly known as Lokkigundi, yielded Neolithic remains at the Kote Veerabhadreshwara complex?
x: Lakkundi in Gadag district, Karnataka, was formerly known as Lokkigundi and yielded Neolithic remains at the Kote Veerabhadreshwara complex. Jehanpora and Piprahwa are associated with different archaeological discoveries.

s: For the discovery of what was Jehanpora in Baramulla district, J&K, in the news?
o: A Kushan-era stupa and monastery complex
x: Jehanpora yielded a roughly 2,000-year-old Kushan stupa and monastery complex spread over about 10 acres, linked with the Silk Route and Gandhara.

s: The Bhadrakali Temple inscription at Prabhas Patan (1169 CE) is associated with whose reconstruction of Somnath?
x: The inscription, dated 1169 CE, is associated with Kumarapala's fifth reconstruction of Somnath.

s: Who inaugurated the ₹227-crore redeveloped Batadrava Than in Nagaon district of Assam?
x: Amit Shah inaugurated the ₹227-crore redeveloped Batadrava Than in Nagaon district, Assam. It was not inaugurated by Himanta Biswa Sarma.

s: Srimanta Sankardeva's Neo-Vaishnavism is identified with which doctrine?
x: Sankardeva's Neo-Vaishnavism is Eka-Sarana-Nama-Dharma, centred on Krishna alone and stressing Shravana and Kirtana.

s: Sattriya is stated not to be based on the songs of which group of devotional poets?
x: Sattriya is not based on the songs of Tulsidas, Kabir and Mirabai. The other options replace one of these three names with Madhavdeva, who is associated with Sankardeva rather than being part of this specified group.

s: The sanctum (Jagamohan) of the Konark Sun Temple reopened in 2026 after how many years?
x: The British filled it with sand in 1903–04; it reopened after 122 years.

s: In which year was INTACH established?
x: INTACH was established in 1984; the ASI dates to 1861.

s: Where is Bhirrana, an Indus Valley settlement that may date back about 8,000 years?
x: Bhirrana is in Fatehabad district, Haryana.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Hoysalas:
1. They were feudatories of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyana.
2. Their capital moved from Belur to Dwarasamudra (Halebidu).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the Hoysalas began as feudatories of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyana and moved their capital from Belur to Dwarasamudra.

s: As of January 2026, India has how many World Heritage Sites?
x: As of January 2026, India has 44 World Heritage Sites (Moidams of Assam added in 2024 as the 43rd, Maratha Military Landscapes in 2025 as the 44th) under the World Heritage Convention of 1972.

s: In which State is the 'Buddhist Diamond Triangle' of Lalitgiri, Udayagiri and Ratnagiri?
x: The Diamond Triangle (Jajpur/Cuttack, Odisha) was added to India's Tentative List.

s: Which site of the Buddhist Diamond Triangle is the earliest?
x: Lalitgiri is the earliest, Udayagiri the largest, and Ratnagiri is known for Vajrayana sculptures.

s: Who built the Konark Sun Temple?
x: Konark was built around 1250 CE by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

s: According to tradition, who built the Somnath temple of stone in the Kali yuga?
x: Tradition says Soma built it in gold, Ravana in silver, Krishna in wood and Bhimdev Solanki in stone.

s: INSV Kaundinya, the stitched sailing ship, was inspired by a ship painted at which site?
x: It is based on a 5th-century CE ship in the Ajanta paintings.

s: In which district were the Piprahwa relics of the Buddha found in 1898?
x: The relics were found in 1898 at Piprahwa, Siddharthnagar (UP), linked to Kapilavastu.

s: In which year did K.M. Cariappa become the first Indian Commander-in-Chief, the event marked by Army Day (15 January)?
x: K. M. Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief on 15 January 1949.

s:
Assertion (A): World Braille Day is observed on 4 January.
Reason (R): The United Nations General Assembly approved World Braille Day in 2019.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is true because World Braille Day is observed on 4 January, the birth anniversary of Louis Braille. Reason R is false: the United Nations General Assembly approved it in 2018, and it was observed from 2019.

s: Where did the Ministry of Culture mainly hold Parakram Diwas 2026, marking Netaji's 129th birth anniversary?
x: The Ministry of Culture held Parakram Diwas 2026 in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, along with 13 other locations.

s: What was the theme of the 9th National Siddha Day observed on 6 January 2026?
o: The Power of Youth in Co-Creating Education
x: The theme of the 9th National Siddha Day was “Siddha for Global Health.” The other options are associated with Data Privacy Day, International Day of Education and National Road Safety Week respectively.

s: In 1851, Léon Foucault demonstrated Earth's rotation with his pendulum at which place in Paris?
x: Foucault's pendulum demonstration took place at the Panthéon in Paris, not the Eiffel Tower.

s: Which of the following pairs (January observance – associated fact) is correctly matched?
o: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas – Ten years of Startup India
National Road Safety Week – Gandhi's return from South Africa
National Youth Day – Birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda
x: National Youth Day (12 January) marks Swami Vivekananda's birth anniversary. Pravasi Bharatiya Divas marks Gandhi's return, Road Safety Week follows the 4E model, and Startup Day marked ten years of Startup India.

s: On which date is Parakram Diwas, marking Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's birth anniversary, observed?
x: Parakram Diwas is observed on 23 January; 24 January is the International Day of Education.

s: In which year did Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose escape from house arrest?
x: Netaji escaped house arrest in 1941; he founded the Forward Bloc in 1939.

s: National Girl Child Day is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Promotion of Hindi as the Union’s official language
Promotion of girls’ rights and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
x: National Girl Child Day concerns girls’ rights and is linked to the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao initiative.

s: What was the theme of the 16th National Voters' Day in 2026?
x: The theme of the 16th National Voters' Day in 2026 was 'My India, My Vote'. Its tagline was 'Citizen at the Heart of Indian Democracy'.

s: National Youth Day on 12 January marks the birth anniversary of whom?
x: National Youth Day is observed on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda. The 163rd observance was in 2026.

s: What is the theme of International Data Privacy Day 2026 (28 January)?
x: The 2026 theme is “Privacy by Design”; the day commemorates Convention 108.

s: On which date was India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act enacted?
x: The DPDP Act was enacted on 11 August 2023; the DPDP Rules were notified on 13 November 2025.

s: Under the Cyber Fraud Mitigation Centre, what does the Suspect Registry deal with?
x: The Suspect Registry deals with mule accounts; Sahyog handles takedowns and Samanvaya is the platform.

s: Under which ministry was the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) established in 2018?
x: I4C was established in 2018 under the Ministry of Home Affairs; the IT Rules date to 2021.

s: With what is the Cyber Swachhta Kendra under CERT-In mainly concerned?
o: Maintaining a registry of mule accounts
x: Cyber Swachhta Kendra is CERT-In's botnet cleaning and malware analysis centre.

s: In which year was National Girl Child Day (24 January) launched?
x: National Girl Child Day was launched in 2008; it is linked to Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.

s: In which year was the first National Voters' Day observed?
x: The first National Voters' Day was in 2011; 25 January marks the ECI's establishment in 1950.

s: Which day is observed on 25 January?
x: 25 January is National Voters' Day; 24 January holds Girl Child Day and the Day of Education, and 23 January is Parakram Diwas.

s: In which year did Gandhi return from South Africa, the event marked by Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (9 January)?
x: Gandhi returned from South Africa on 9 January 1915.

s: National Siddha Day (6 January) is observed on the birth anniversary of whom?
x: National Siddha Day marks Sage Agastya's birth anniversary; the 9th edition in 2026 had the theme "Siddha for Global Health".

s: What was the theme of the 37th National Road Safety Week (11–17 January 2026)?
x: The 37th National Road Safety Week's theme was "Sadak Suraksha, Jeevan Raksha", based on the 4E model.

s: Which body instituted International Data Privacy Day (Data Protection Day) in 2006?
x: The Council of Europe instituted it in 2006; it marks Convention 108, opened for signature on 28 January 1981.

s: National Startup Day 2026 (16 January) marked how many years of Startup India?
x: National Startup Day 2026 marked 10 years of Startup India.

s:
Consider the following statements about the NDRF:
1. It was established on 19 January 2006.
2. Its Raising Day has been observed since 2007.
3. It was set up under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the NDRF was established on 19 January 2006 under the DM Act, 2005, and its Raising Day has been observed since 2007.

s: In which year was the Election Commission of India established, the date marked by National Voters' Day?
x: The ECI was set up on 25 January 1950; National Voters' Day has been observed since 2011.

s:
Arrange the following January days in calendar order:
1. National Voters' Day
2. Parakram Diwas
3. National Youth Day
4. Army Day
x: National Youth Day 12 Jan, Army Day 15 Jan, Parakram Diwas 23 Jan, National Voters' Day 25 Jan.

s: Whom did K.M. Cariappa replace as Commander-in-Chief on 15 January 1949, the event marked by Army Day?
x: Cariappa took over from General Sir Roy Bucher, the last British C-in-C.

s: International Data Privacy Day (28 January) marks the opening for signature of which treaty?
x: It marks Council of Europe Convention 108 (28 January 1981), the first binding international data protection treaty.

s: When were the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules notified?
x: The DPDP Act was enacted on 11 August 2023 and the DPDP Rules were notified on 13 November 2025.

s: What is the national cybercrime helpline number run by I4C?
x: I4C (2018, MHA) runs the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and helpline 1930.

s: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
x: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force on 26 January 1950.

s: What was the theme of the 77th Republic Day celebrations in 2026?
x: The theme of the 77th Republic Day celebrations was “150 Years of Vande Mataram.” “Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram” and “Samriddhi ka Mantra – Atmanirbhar Bharat” were parade themes, while “Operation Sindoor – Victory Through Jointness” was the Tri-Services tableau theme.

s: Which battalion took part in the Republic Day parade for the first time in 2026?
x: The Bhairav Light Commando Battalion debuted at the 2026 parade.

s: At the 77th Republic Day parade (2026), which State's tableau featured Madam Bhikaji Cama and the evolution of the National Flag?
x: Gujarat's tableau featured Madam Bhikaji Cama and the evolution of the National Flag (1906–1947). Maharashtra showed Ganeshotsav as a social movement and West Bengal the origins of Vande Mataram.

s: At the 77th Republic Day parade (2026), which State's tableau marked Guru Tegh Bahadur's 350th martyrdom year?
x: Punjab's tableau marked Guru Tegh Bahadur's 350th martyrdom year; Kerala showed the Kochi Water Metro and 100% digital literacy.

s: Which of the following pairs (Republic Day parade 2026 category – winner) is correctly matched?
o: Best tableau among Ministries – Ministry of Culture
x: The Ministry of Culture won among Ministries; the Indian Navy won the Services category and Delhi Police the CAPF/auxiliary category.

s: Who were the Chief Guests at the 77th Republic Day celebrations in 2026?
o: Charles Michel and Ursula von der Leyen
Ursula von der Leyen and Roberta Metsola
Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa
x: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa were the Chief Guests.

s: In the Rajya Sabha debate on 150 years of Vande Mataram, who demanded that it get the same constitutional status as the national anthem?
x: Leader of the House J.P. Nadda made the demand; Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of distorting history.

s: During which movement was Vande Mataram popularised?
x: Vande Mataram was popularised during the Swadeshi agitation of 1905.

s: What did Gandhi write in Harijan (July 1939) should be done if anyone objected to Vande Mataram in a mixed gathering?
o: Only the first two stanzas should be sung
Only the first stanza should be sung
x: Gandhi said it should be dropped if anyone objected; singing the first two stanzas was Tagore's view.

s: On which date was Vande Mataram first published, whose 150 years the February 2026 guidelines marked?
x: Vande Mataram was first published on 7 November 1875; 2025-26 marked 150 years of it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the MHA guidelines on Vande Mataram issued on 6 February 2026?
o: All six stanzas are sung at official functions and educational institutions
It is mandatory to stand in cinema halls when Vande Mataram is played
Everyone remains standing attentively while it is sung at official functions
When both are played, Vande Mataram is played first, followed by the National Anthem
x: Standing in cinema halls is not mandatory under the guidelines.

s: Under the MHA guidelines, how long does singing all six stanzas of Vande Mataram take?
x: All six stanzas take 3 minutes 10 seconds, and everyone stands attentively.

s: Who was the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly?
x: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the permanent President, and M.N. Roy proposed the idea of a Constituent Assembly.

s: On which date was Vande Mataram designated the national song in the Constituent Assembly?
x: Dr Rajendra Prasad designated Vande Mataram the national song on 24 January 1950, with equal status to Jana Gana Mana.

s: Following the Lahore Session of 1929 (presided over by Nehru), which date was observed as Purna Swaraj Day?
x: The Lahore Session demanded Purna Swaraj, and 26 January 1930 was observed as Purna Swaraj Day.

s: On which date did the Constituent Assembly of India first meet?
x: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946; it completed its work in 11 sessions over 165 days.

s: Which two words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976?
x: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 added the words “Socialist” and “Secular.” The other options do not identify the two words specified in this constitutional amendment.

s: How many Padma Awards were announced in 2026?
x: 131 Padma Awards were announced: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri.

s: In which language did Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay originally write Vande Mataram?
x: Vande Mataram was written in Sanskrit, not Bengali; it was first published on 7 November 1875.

s: What do Article 51A(a) and the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 cover?
o: The National Flag and Anthem only
The National Flag, Anthem and Song
x: They cover the Flag and the Anthem only, not the National Song.

s: Which State's tableau won first place among State/UT tableaux at the 77th Republic Day parade?
x: Maharashtra won first place, followed by Jammu & Kashmir and Kerala; Gujarat topped the People's Choice.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:
1. The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first put forward by M.N. Roy.
2. Its permanent President was Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
3. It held 12 sessions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct; the Assembly held 11 sessions over 165 days.

s: Which of the following about Vande Mataram is NOT correct?
o: It was authored by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
It appeared in the novel Anandamath.
It was popularised during the Swadeshi agitation of 1905.
It was adopted as the National Anthem of India.
x: Vande Mataram, by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, appeared in Anandamath (1882) and became popular during the Swadeshi agitation of 1905. It was adopted as the National Song (24 January 1950), not the National Anthem, which is Jana Gana Mana.

s: Which of the following about the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, is NOT correct?
o: It covers the national song, Vande Mataram.
It is a law concerning national honour.
x: The Act covers the National Flag and the National Anthem but not the national song.

s: Which first took place at the 77th Republic Day parade (2026)?
o: A foreign military contingent marched for the first time
The EU military contingent took part, its first such participation outside Europe
The parade moved to Kartavya Path
x: In 2026 an EU military contingent marched – the EU's first such participation outside Europe.

s: Which Army unit formed the first animal contingent at the Republic Day parade 2026?
x: The Remount and Veterinary Corps (est. 1889) brought Bactrian camels, horses, eagles and dogs.

s: Which contingent won the best marching contingent award among the Services at the 77th Republic Day parade?
x: The Indian Navy won best marching contingent (Services); Delhi Police won among CAPF/auxiliary forces.

s: In which year did the Congress Working Committee decide that only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram be sung at national gatherings?
x: The 1937 CWC decided on the first two stanzas only.

s: During which period was NACP I, India's first comprehensive HIV/AIDS programme, implemented?
x: NACP I ran from 1992 to 1999; NACP III ran from 2007 to 2012 and NACP V from 2021 to 2026.

s: What was the theme of World AIDS Day observed on December 1, 2025?
o: Overcoming disruption, transforming the AIDS response
x: The theme of World AIDS Day 2025 was “Overcoming disruption, transforming the AIDS response.” “End AIDS by 2030” is the goal under the WHO strategy, while “Halt and reverse by 2012” was associated with NACP III.

s: Who presided over the AITUC in 1920?
x: The AITUC in 1920 was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai, not S.A. Dange.

s: With which region was the Tebhaga movement, a peasant movement of the 1940s, associated?
x: Tebhaga was a Bengal peasant movement; during 1942–45 the CPI backed the anti-Fascist war over Quit India.

s: Which initiative aims to bring back people living with HIV who were lost to follow-up on ART?
x: Bringing back people living with HIV lost to follow-up on ART is the objective of Mission Sampark.

s: To which place and year does the CPI(M) trace the origin of the communist party in India?
x: The CPI(M) traces its origin to Tashkent in 1920, while the CPI counts the Kanpur Conference of 1925.

s: Within how much time of exposure should HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be taken?
x: PEP should be taken within 72 hours of exposure.

s: Which cultural practice was identified as India’s next nomination after Diwali for UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage process?
x: Chhath Puja of Bihar was identified as the next nomination. Yoga, Ramman and Vedic Chanting were listed as earlier Indian elements, not the next nomination.

s: Since which year has Yoga been on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage?
x: Yoga has been on UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage list since 2016.

s: In 2025, Diwali became India's which element on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
x: Diwali became India's 16th element on the list in 2025.

s: In which year was Kumbh Mela inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
x: Kumbh Mela was inscribed in 2017, not 2018; Durga Puja in Kolkata followed in 2021.

s: Which of the following pairs related to HIV is correctly matched?
